actual_scope: Under the zero-swap, one-scale hypotheses of the helper-462 rank-drop argument, can the elementary shear lower bound of 9 be raised to 10?
scope_change_reason: The catalogue card asks a supplier-admission question. This package takes the allowed one-proposition variation and answers the named open question from PR #7125: whether the rank-drop floor of 9 for a one-scale zero-swap word in the pinned helper-462 matcher can be raised to 10. It does not admit a supplier and does not change the selected frontier.
bottleneck_link: Side result on the pinned helper-462 matcher. It raises an elementary-word lower bound and does not change the selected kappa or a paid profile.
stop_rule: Stop when every scale row's rank-drop census is certified and every rank-preserving elementary shear of every census matrix of rank 6, 7 or 8 has depth strictly below that rank, or when one such shear meets the rank and supplies a length-9 word.
evidence: research/helper462-one-scale-shear-floor-10/README.md and verify.py. The length-9 shape is proved, and the stall search is a finite pencil certificate.
author: unpaidmoon

open_questions.question: Is 10 sharp for a one-scale zero-swap elementary word in the pinned helper-462 matcher, or does a second obstruction force length at least 11?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The certificate rules out length 9. The recorded upper bound is the 21-shear word of PR #7125, so the integers 10 through 21 stay open. A word of length 10 would show that 10 is sharp.
open_questions.first_step: Classify a length-10 word: the rank changes sum to 8 over 10 steps of size at most 1, so either there are two rank-preserving shears or one descent and one stall. The same census is the place to look.
open_questions.blocked_by: A non-dropping shear has a free rational coefficient. The length-9 case split does not cover two stalls, and no length-10 word is known.
